chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from al-Sulayman al-Ja'fari, that Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:
Pray one hundred units of prayer on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, reciting 'Al-Hamd' once and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' ten times in each unit.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed prayer ritual for the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* outlines a specific devotional practice for the 21st and 23rd nights of Ramadan, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha once and Surah Al-Ikhlas ten times per unit. This ritual is traditionally linked to the martyrdom of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) on the 21st night and his final burial on the 23rd, serving as a spiritual preparation for the night of Laylat al-Qadr. The emphasis on Al-Ikhlas highlights the theological core of Tawhid, which Shia scholars often associate with the purity of heart required during these pivotal nights.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 20-6 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Al-Hussein ibn al-Hassan ibn Aban quoted Al-Hassan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Suleiman al-Ja’fari that Abul Hassan Al-Kadhim (MGB) said, “

Say one-hundred units of prayers on the 21st and 23rd nights of the month of Ramazan. Say the Opening Chapter (Al-Fatiha ) once in each unit and say the Al-Ikhlas Chapter ten times in each unit of these prayers.”
